headline: Readiness verdict is red — 38.7, HRV-driven — after a load spike and a missed long run. Today is truly easy, no exceptions.
body_state: The deterministic verdict is red: readiness composite **38.7**, driver **HRV** — it's below your personal band even though Garmin's own daily badge still says Balanced (37 ms last night; the trend overrides the badge here). Body Battery bottomed at **18** this morning — recovery didn't happen overnight. Sleep was 7.5 h (score 75), but 14-day debt is still **20 h**. Resting HR **52** vs your 48.7 baseline. Acute:chronic load ratio is **2.01** — well past the 1.5 threshold where injury risk doubles — driven by three straight days of unplanned indoor cardio, not running. TSB −5.25 sits in the nominally 'productive' band, but the recovery side overrides that today.
session: Plan calls for **4 km Easy + 6 Strides**. Run the 3.7 km easy leg at 4:35–5:03/km, HR capped around 136–145. Skip the strides — Body Battery 18 and the red verdict say hold all quality, and strides are exactly what the plan's own fallback line covers: 'feeling forced or heavy-legged? cut them.' If today's Outdoor Cycling block happens too, keep it conversational, not a session — you don't have recovery budget for two loaded efforts today.
recent: Yesterday's 5 km Long Run was missed outright — nothing logged. The three days before it were all unplanned indoor cardio: Jul 29 genuinely hard (48% Z4/Z5, HR to 190), then Jul 30 and Aug 1 both grey-zone (44% and 38% in Z3, HR 130–136 avg) — none rated in RPE. That's your #1 flagged limiter in the data — 16% easy vs an 80% target — and it's exactly what's driving today's load spike despite almost no real running this week (13.2 km rolling).
focus: Protect today: easy only, no strides, no hard cycling — HRV and Body Battery both say no.
Rate the last three cardio sessions in the app (Jul 29, 30, Aug 1) — none have an RPE, and HR-based load likely understates them.
Get to bed ~60 min earlier tonight — 20 h of sleep debt over two weeks is the actual bottleneck, not fitness.
